title: LFAST: an LLM agent drives robotic synthesis of the new COF-2000 framework
summary: A GPT-4o-based agent (LFAST) screened reaction conditions over a 96-condition matrix and refined them after each round, raising the crystallinity index of a reference covalent organic framework by 350% and yielding COF-2000, a previously unreported material with higher structural order. The reported validation is crystallinity measurement of the synthesized products; the authors do not pursue applications. Publication date is taken from secondary reports of the JACS paper and should be checked against the journal page.
ai_technology: LFAST (LLM For Accelerated Synthesis Technique), GPT-4o agent with robotic experimentation

evidence.tested: Products of LFAST-guided conditions characterized by powder X-ray diffraction: crystallinity index raised by 350% on the benchmark COF TpPa-SO3H; COF-2000 characterized by PXRD and crystallinity index only.
evidence.unknown: Evidence rests on one benchmark system and one new COF; the full text was not read, so limitations discussed there are unknown.
evidence.ai_role: LLM deep research agent mined the literature for synthesis conditions; an automated platform ran them and PXRD analyzed the products.
